items.headline: Bitdeer AI adds 60MW (A103) in Cyberjaya under an 8-year services agreement; campus to reach ~71.5MW
items.detail: A103 is designed for liquid-cooled NVIDIA rack-scale systems, with energisation expected in 1Q2028. The Cyberjaya campus would total about 71.5MW of AI cloud capacity (critical IT load), per the company.

sources.publisher: Bitdeer AI press release (GlobeNewswire via Nasdaq)

items.note: Released 12 Oct 2026 4:30pm EDT (13 Oct MYT). Company-stated figures; timeline is a forecast.
items.soWhat: Malaysia is winning the next generation of liquid-cooled AI capacity, not just conventional colocation.
items.opportunity: Demand for liquid-cooling, power and fit-out contractors on the Cyberjaya campus.
items.watchOut: Energisation targeted for 1Q2028, a company forecast.

items.headline: Deep Source locks in 10-year colocation for 67MW AI data centre in Prai, Penang; 26MW due by Mar 2027
items.detail: Deep Source (PN) signed a master colocation agreement on 2 Oct covering 67MW, plus a 7 Oct letter of intent with Longmotive DC Solutions for building and M&E works: 26MW targeted by 31 Mar 2027 and 41MW by 30 Jun 2027.
items.note: Customer not named. Completion dates are targets, subject to certification.
items.soWhat: Penang is emerging as an AI data-centre node beyond Johor and Klang Valley.
items.opportunity: Building and M&E works (LOI with Longmotive) point to near-term fit-out demand.
items.watchOut: Customer unnamed; completion subject to certification.

items.headline: Realord signs MOU for a possible Johor AI data centre of up to 300MW (first phase ~100MW)
items.detail: Phased project, first phase about 100MW; involves land acquisition in Johor and is subject to definitive agreements and regulatory approvals.
items.note: Status: MOU only; the company warns it may not materialise.
items.soWhat: Signals continued foreign interest in Johor capacity, but nothing is committed.
items.watchOut: Proposal only: non-binding MOU, subject to land, definitive agreements and approvals.

items.headline: MITI approves Privasia unit's Bagan Datuk data centre, conditional on off-grid power of up to 50MW
items.detail: Approval (letter dated 7 Sept 2026) is conditional on securing an off-grid energy supply with maximum demand of 50MW, in line with Energy Commission and RE frameworks.
items.soWhat: Approvals now hinge on power sourcing; off-grid supply is becoming a precondition.
items.watchOut: Subject to securing off-grid energy within Energy Commission and RE frameworks.

items.headline: 27 data centre projects worth RM225.97bil approved under the DCTF to July 2026; 16 in Johor, 10 in Selangor, one operating
items.detail: Digital Ministry written reply: 4,053 jobs expected (3,523 high-skilled); projects carry a 30% minimum local-content requirement monitored by MIDA.
items.soWhat: The approved pipeline is large and mostly still under construction, so fit-out, M&E and power work has years to run.
items.opportunity: The 30% local-content rule favours Malaysian contractors, cable and M&E suppliers.
items.watchOut: Only one of the 27 projects is operating; delivery depends on power and water hook-ups.

items.headline: Princeton Digital Group reportedly seeks up to US$1.2bil (RM4.9bil) three-year loan for 198.8MW Johor campus
items.detail: Reported three-year syndicated loan, citing an unnamed source; borrower Princeton Digital Group Labuan Alpha Ltd. Arrangers: HSBC (Singapore), Maybank IB, OCBC Malaysia, StanChart (Singapore) and UOB. Proceeds also refinance existing debt.
items.soWhat: Debt is now funding Johor hyperscale capacity at scale, with Maybank IB among the lead arrangers.
items.watchOut: Unconfirmed: the company and banks did not comment.

items.headline: Madani Submarine Cable (Salam) to start 1Q2027 and finish 4Q2029; Jendela 2 Group 1 rolls out 1,000 sites from November
items.detail: Communications Ministry written reply in Parliament. Jendela 2 Group 1 includes 352 sites in Sabah.
items.soWhat: Two sizeable telco infrastructure programmes are moving, with MCMC now evaluating Salam submissions.
items.opportunity: Tender pipeline for submarine cable, tower and fibre contractors.
items.watchOut: Salam is still at evaluation stage; no award announced.

items.headline: Hibiscus Petroleum and Seri Pajam to evaluate on-site gas, solar and carbon-capture power for data centres at SPD Tech Valley, Senawang
items.detail: Collaboration agreement dated 30 Sept; framework to assess deployment, not an investment commitment.
items.soWhat: Another sign that on-site power is becoming part of the data-centre offer as grid capacity tightens.

items.headline: RedPlanet IPO public tranche oversubscribed 85.28 times (1.77bil shares, ~RM336.72mil applied) ahead of LEAP-to-ACE move on 22 Oct
items.detail: Figures refer to the Malaysian public portion only.
items.soWhat: Strong retail demand for a geospatial and rail ICT provider shows appetite for small-cap tech listings.
items.watchOut: Heavy oversubscription can mean volatile early trading.

items.headline: Infomina 1Q net profit rises to RM10.55mil from RM8.08mil; revenue up to RM76.19mil from RM54.63mil
items.detail: Quarter to 31 Aug 2026, led by technology infrastructure O&M.
items.soWhat: Tech-infrastructure operations and maintenance is driving growth, a sign of steady outsourcing demand.

items.headline: DayOne secures extra RM15bil (US$3.7bil) from seven banks for Johor data centres; financing platform doubles to RM30bil
items.detail: The add-on comprises a US$2.4bil offshore term loan and a RM5.5bil Murabahah facility, arranged by CIMB, Credit Agricole CIB, DBS, Maybank, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB. It follows a RM15bil multi-currency facility in 2025.
items.note: Per a joint lenders' statement on 13 Oct. DealStreetAsia listed as corroborating source (paywalled; not fully read).
items.soWhat: Bank appetite for Johor hyperscale debt is deepening: one operator now has RM30bil of committed financing, well above PDG's reported US$1.2bil loan.
items.opportunity: Local banks (CIMB, Maybank) gain large DC project-finance exposure; contractors and M&E suppliers gain funded pipeline.
items.watchOut: Concentration risk for lenders if power and water reviews slow Johor projects.

items.headline: Govt reviewing data centres' actual power and water needs; deputy minister says operators could be required to build own solar and storage
items.detail: Deputy Energy Transition Minister Abdul Rahman Mohamad told the Dewan Rakyat that data centres reserve more power than they use. An MP raised five-year take-or-pay supply contracts. Malaysia had ~14,000MW of RE capacity (~32%) at 1 Sept; 10,000-11,000MW more is scheduled by 2030.
items.note: Parliamentary answer; self-generation is a possibility raised by the minister, not an adopted rule.
items.soWhat: Contracted-versus-used power is now a policy issue, so future DC approvals and tariffs may tighten.
items.watchOut: Possible self-supply or selection criteria could raise DC project costs.

items.headline: BNM and SC warn of deepfake videos impersonating their senior officers to promote investment schemes
items.detail: Public directed to bnm.gov.my/verify, BNM's Financial Consumer Alert List, the SC Investor Alert List, BNMLINK and the SC Investment Checker.
items.note: Regulator advisory; no losses or cases quantified.
items.soWhat: AI-enabled impersonation is now targeting regulators' own brand; financial firms face the same fraud risk with customers.
items.watchOut: Brand-impersonation and customer-fraud exposure for banks and lenders.

items.headline: EcoSys jumps up to 179% on ACE Market debut after RM39.34mil IPO; Bursa's top traded counter
items.detail: Hit 75.5 sen intraday vs 27 sen IPO price; 73 sen at the time of reporting on 96.45mil shares traded. Proceeds go to the abatement segment, ultra-high-purity fabrication and India expansion.
items.note: Intraday morning prices; closing price not verified.
items.soWhat: Strong retail appetite for semiconductor-services IPOs, alongside RedPlanet's oversubscription.
items.watchOut: Debut-day premiums can fade.

items.headline: Data-centre power works: MN Holdings wins RM293.88mil for two 275kV landing stations; Kinergy gets RM47.5mil Gamuda subcontract in Port Dickson
items.detail: MN Holdings' unit will build two 275kV consumer landing stations for an unnamed data-hosting client in central Peninsular Malaysia (Sept 2026-Aug 2027). Kinergy Advancement will do core-and-shell electrical works for a hyperscale DC in Bandar Spring Hill for a US tech firm, due 1Q2028.
items.note: Two separate Bursa-filed awards combined; clients unnamed. MN figure includes SST.
items.soWhat: High-voltage grid connection is a growing contract pool for electrical specialists.
items.opportunity: HV substation and electrical subcontract demand from DC developers.

items.headline: Budget 2027 digital targets: 200,000 skilled AI professionals, MDEC funding for 4,000 MSMEs to adopt AI, 100,000 more free AI subscriptions
items.detail: Per the Ministry of Digital's post-budget statement: training and certification for 5,000 AI professionals, AI Malaysia Bhd to be strengthened, 16,000+ free Coursera courses via Rakyat Digital, DE Rantau pass extended by two years.
items.note: Announced targets; application details not yet published.
items.soWhat: State-funded AI adoption for SMEs creates demand for AI integrators and training providers.

items.headline: MOSTI gets RM1.29bil for 2027 (+1.29%): RM41mil to Cradle for 5,500-startup roadmap, RM10mil for SemiconStart follow-on equity
items.detail: Split: RM775.46mil operating, RM516.93mil development, 61 projects. Also RM10mil for KMP's FORGE pilot and RM2mil for a plantation IoT/robotics programme.
items.note: Ministry allocation statement.
items.soWhat: Allocations are small relative to private DC capex; the signal is continuity, not a step-up.

items.headline: Genting Malaysia signs MoU with Alibaba Cloud to explore AI and cloud across its operations
items.detail: Signed in Hangzhou; builds on an earlier Genting SkyWorlds pilot. Covers productivity, operations and guest experience; no projects, timelines or deployment commitments disclosed.
items.note: MoU only; non-binding.
items.soWhat: Large leisure operators are testing hyperscaler AI tools; no committed spend yet.

items.headline: U Mobile signs MoU with HLGY Energy to explore private 5G for smart solar farms under CRESS
items.detail: Private 5G would support drone inspections, AI analytics and CCTV at HLGY's utility-scale solar assets, including the Kedah Rubber City solar plant.
items.note: MoU only; no value disclosed. Company press content.
items.soWhat: Telcos are pitching private 5G into renewable-energy assets as an enterprise revenue line.

items.headline: S P Setia (2Q26 sales RM864mil) backs Budget 2027 first-home relief up to RM750,000 and Johor focus
items.detail: Cites the first-home stamp-duty relief up to RM750,000 to 2030, JS-SEZ focus and Green Investment Tax Allowance for its Setia Fontaines Industrial Park. 2Q26 sales were RM864mil; net profit RM98.06mil (2Q25: RM99.8mil).
items.soWhat: A large developer reads the Budget as supportive for townships and Johor industrial land.
items.opportunity: JS-SEZ and Green Investment Tax Allowance support industrial park plays such as Setia Fontaines.
items.watchOut: 2Q26 net profit dipped to RM98.06mil from RM99.8mil.

items.headline: Budget 2027: first-home stamp duty waived up to RM500,000, and on the first RM500,000 of homes up to RM750,000, for 2027-2030 SPAs
items.detail: Full exemption up to RM500,000; for RM500,001-RM750,000, the first RM500,000 is fully exempt and the balance 50%. Abandoned-project revivals get full exemption; SJKP guarantees of up to RM20bil target about 80,000 first-time buyers. KPKT says SJKP has helped over 100,000 buyers, with guarantees of up to 120% that can cover renovation and furnishing.
items.note: Proposals; effective subject to the Finance Bill.
items.soWhat: Lowers buyers' upfront cash need in the core mass-market band; RM20bil SJKP guarantees widen the pool to ~80,000 self-employed first-time buyers.
items.opportunity: Products priced at or below RM750,000 for first-time buyers.
items.watchOut: Proposal only, subject to the Finance Bill; applies to Malaysian citizens' first homes.

items.headline: Rehda asks government to extend first-home stamp-duty relief to homes up to RM1mil
items.detail: Developers' association welcomed the Budget housing measures but said material, labour and regulatory costs keep pressuring affordability.
items.soWhat: Industry signals costs, not demand, are the affordability bottleneck.
items.watchOut: Rising material, labour and regulatory charges continue to pressure margins.

items.headline: KPKT says 1,726 sick and abandoned housing projects worth RM158.16bil GDV revived as at end-August
items.detail: Nearly 200,000 homes completed, back on track or resolved. KL still has seven abandoned private projects and 12 sick projects involving 6,102 buyers.
items.soWhat: Clearing the abandoned-project backlog supports buyer confidence and frees stuck land and contractors.
items.watchOut: Completion timelines depend on each project; some are tied up in court.

items.headline: RHB keeps property Overweight: developers trade at 60% discount to RNAV (51% in May); Eco World top pick, TP RM2.66
items.detail: RHB says negatives are priced in; Budget stamp-duty relief to 2030 helps Matrix, Mah Sing and LBS; Iskandar names (Eco World, UEM Sunrise, Sunway, Mah Sing, AME) set to benefit from the JS-SEZ masterplan due in December. 2Q26 property sales +32% y-o-y.
items.note: Analyst view (RHB Research); target price is a forecast.
items.soWhat: Valuations are deeply discounted; the JS-SEZ masterplan in December is the next catalyst.
items.watchOut: Higher mortgage costs and softer mass-market demand.

items.headline: Mitraland launches RM800mil GDV Bayou Quartz in Klang; Phase 1A 90% taken up
items.detail: 52-acre freehold landed scheme; Phase 1 has 287 garden and park villas from RM905,000. Phase 1A (118 units) 90% taken up since the August soft launch; Phase 1B (169 units) opened.
items.note: Unlisted developer; take-up is company-reported.
items.soWhat: Demand for landed homes near RM1mil remains firm in the Klang Valley.

items.headline: IJM wins RM1.23bil AT&S semiconductor plant in Kulim; order book rises to ~RM10.6bil
items.detail: Design-and-build of production, central utility and wastewater buildings; starts 4Q2026 with a 14-month programme. Order book about RM10.6bil after the award, following RM909.5mil of semiconductor and medtech wins in August.
items.note: IJM cites its IBS capabilities for delivery.
items.soWhat: Semiconductor fast-track builds are becoming a large, repeatable contract pool for top-tier contractors.
items.opportunity: Follows RM909.5mil of August semiconductor/medtech wins; IBS used for delivery certainty.
items.watchOut: Tight 14-month programme from 4Q2026.

items.headline: GDB proposes RM81.6mil buy of 51% of two Sarawak contractors, lifting order book to RM741.81mil
items.detail: Consideration RM40.8mil cash plus 96.91 million shares at 42 sen; vendors guarantee cumulative PAT of at least RM45mil (Jul 2026-Dec 2028). Order book would rise to RM741.81mil. GDB also plans entry into property development with a RM500mil GDV Kuching project.
items.note: Status: proposed; gross proceeds RM70.83mil-RM183.48mil depending on take-up. Dilution is a watch-out.
items.soWhat: Scales GDB into Sarawak and property development (RM500mil GDV Kuching project).
items.opportunity: Vendors guarantee cumulative PAT of at least RM45mil for Jul 2026-Dec 2028.
items.watchOut: Proposal only; funded by placement of up to 30% plus rights issue, so dilution.

items.headline: Budget 2027 reintroduces the variation-of-price mechanism for construction inputs such as diesel and bitumen
items.detail: Says the mechanism will help contractors manage swings in inputs such as diesel and bitumen.
items.soWhat: Reduces contractors' exposure to input-cost swings on public jobs.
items.watchOut: Scope and eligible contracts not detailed in the source.

items.headline: Gamuda-MiTAC JV wins RM3.72bil (NT$29.22bil) Keelung MRT trackwork and systems contract in Taiwan; Gamuda share RM2.7bil
items.detail: Gamuda holds 72.84% of the JV; awarded by New Taipei City Government; 15.6km, 13 stations. Contribution expected from FY ending July 2027 (company statement).
items.soWhat: Adds overseas order book for Malaysia's largest contractor over 7.7 years, keeping domestic capacity free for local jobs.

items.headline: AWC wins RM39.7mil plumbing, water and sanitary subcontract from Gamuda Engineering for a Port Dickson hyperscale data centre
items.detail: Awarded to unit Qudotech for cold water, rainwater harvesting, fire hydrant and sanitary works in Bandar Springhill. Works started 14 Aug; completion due 22 Oct 2027; revenue from FY27. Fourth data-centre job in 12 months (combined RM127.3mil); order book RM824.3mil at 30 June 2026, excluding this job.
items.soWhat: Data-centre work is filtering down to specialist M&E subcontractors, not just main contractors.

items.headline: Inta Bina files proposed development by wholly-owned subsidiary Seiring Setia Sdn Bhd
items.soWhat: A new development plan from a watchlist contractor; size and terms are in the filing.
items.note: Bursa filing; details not summarised.

items.headline: Pesona Metro filed 14 share buy-back notices between 1 and 14 Oct
items.soWhat: Ongoing buy-backs; watch for any change in the pace or size of purchases.
items.note: Based on the company's Bursa announcement list (company filter, 1-14 Oct), read in the browser.

items.headline: Palm oil stocks jump 24.54% to 3.51mil tonnes in September; exports fall 12.13% to 1.12mil t
items.detail: CPO production rose 16.48% m-o-m to 2.117mil t; palm oil exports fell 12.13% to 1.120mil t; CPO stocks up 31.88% to 2.163mil t.
items.note: Preliminary data.
items.soWhat: Inventory overhang caps near-term CPO prices.
items.watchOut: Preliminary MPOB data.

items.headline: Kenanga holds 2027 CPO assumption at RM4,700/t despite 10-year-high stocks; sector kept at Neutral
items.detail: Analyst view: inventory 3.511mil t (+49% y-o-y); CPO assumptions RM4,500/t (2026) and RM4,700/t (2027), citing biodiesel demand and El Nino supply risk in 2027; warns of cost inflation.
items.note: Analyst estimates, not reported facts.
items.soWhat: Analyst view: biodiesel demand and El Nino could tighten 2027 supply.
items.watchOut: Forecast only; cost inflation risk to margins.

items.headline: Malaysia-EU FTA 80% done, signing targeted by end-June 2027; palm oil and autos unresolved
items.detail: MITI minister Johari Abdul Ghani targets signing by end-June 2027 and says major producers are preparing for the EUDR.
items.note: Target date is a government aim, not a commitment.
items.soWhat: EU market access for palm oil remains contingent on EUDR compliance.
items.opportunity: Major producers say they already meet EUDR requirements.
items.watchOut: Target date is a government aim, not a commitment.

items.headline: Phillip Capital sees CPO at RM4,350-4,800/t in 4Q26; lifts 2026E average to RM4,470/t, sector Neutral, SDG top pick
items.detail: 2027E raised to RM4,500/t. Sector earnings now seen +3.6% in 2026E and +6.4% in 2027E. Inventories +48.8% y-o-y; refining margins pressured by Indonesian competition.
items.note: Analyst forecasts.
items.soWhat: Firm prices are being offset by costs; a re-rating is not expected.

items.headline: CIMB: RM2,000 minimum wage from June 2027 could cut planters' FY28 earnings by up to 7%
items.detail: Estimated hit 0.2-4% in FY27 and 2-7% in FY28; most exposed are Johor Plantations, Ta Ann and Hap Seng Plantations. CIMB keeps Overweight on El Niño supply risk; top picks IOI, KLK, Genting Plantations, Hap Seng Plantations.
items.note: Analyst estimate; assumes over half of estate workers affected.
items.soWhat: Labour-cost step-up will accelerate mechanisation.
items.opportunity: Suppliers of agricultural machinery and automation.
items.watchOut: Upstream planters with high general-worker share.

items.headline: Budget 2027: RM100mil hybrid financing for 4,500 oil palm smallholders to replant, only half repayable
items.detail: Also RM30mil for crop disease and pests (Ganoderma, bagworms, mealybugs), RM100mil for estate roads, and rubber production incentive raised to RM3.30/kg for 300,000+ smallholders.
items.note: Budget proposal.
items.soWhat: Supports long-term smallholder yields; limited near-term earnings effect for listed planters.

items.headline: Budget 2027 lifts loan and financing guarantees to RM57bil (from RM50bil); SJPP limit raised to RM50mil for mid-tier firms
items.detail: BNM doubles its West Asia-affected SME facility to RM10bil; BPMB allocates RM7bil across seven sectors; SJPP and CGC provide up to RM32bil in guarantees, with RM1bil of SJPP for M&A.
items.note: Budget proposal; this covers SME and corporate financing, not licensed moneylending specifically.
items.soWhat: Government-guaranteed credit competes with, and de-risks, private SME lending.
items.watchOut: Cheaper guaranteed loans may crowd out non-bank lenders.

items.headline: Budget 2027 gives RM1,500 one-off aid to 1.3mil civil servants and RM750 to pensioners, in two instalments
items.detail: Covers Grade Utama B and below, including contract staff; instalments before Aidilfitri and ahead of the 70th Merdeka anniversary.
items.note: Interpretation: a one-off cash boost to civil-servant borrowers' disposable income, not a financing measure.
items.soWhat: Interpretation: modestly improves repayment capacity of civil-servant borrowers.
items.watchOut: One-off cash aid, not a financing measure; paid before Aidilfitri and before the 70th Merdeka anniversary.

items.headline: CTOS cyber breach: CTOS Score and CCRIS-related reports still down; FY2026 profit hit estimated at RM12mil
items.detail: Company estimate assumes some services stay unavailable until the third week of October; each extra week cuts profit by about RM1.3mil.
items.soWhat: Lenders that rely on CTOS/CCRIS reports for credit checks face slower or riskier approvals until services return.
items.watchOut: Check whether your credit-assessment process has a fallback while reports are unavailable.

items.headline: Budget 2027 commits RM15bil via TNB to the grid; industry warns grid and storage gaps could slow RE
items.detail: Also cites UEM Lestra RM1bil for projects incl. KLIA energy storage and a 1GW Johor hybrid project; green tech tax incentives extended to 31 Dec 2030.
items.note: Interpretation: grid capex is a demand driver for cable makers, but the article does not name any cable company.
items.soWhat: Interpretation: grid capex is a direct demand driver for power-cable makers.
items.opportunity: Grid, BESS and the 1GW Johor hybrid project imply cable call-ups.
items.watchOut: Article names no cable company; pace depends on connection approvals.

items.headline: HLIB lifts Southern Cable target to RM3.58; RM200mil DC and 132kV orders fill FY26 MV/HV capacity
items.detail: Analyst view: RM200mil of 2Q26 DC and 132kV orders have fully booked MV/HV capacity for FY26; 3Q26 revenue could reach RM600mil and FY26 sales top RM2bil.
items.note: Analyst estimates. Watch-out: higher plastic costs squeeze margins on TNB orders.
items.soWhat: Analyst view: data-centre orders are shifting the mix away from TNB.
items.watchOut: Higher plastic costs squeeze TNB-order margins.

items.headline: Government reportedly lifts CRESS grid access charge to 18 sen/kWh from the 14 sen announced in September; ex-minister warns of investor fallout
items.detail: Raised by Yeo Bee Yin in the Budget 2027 debate, citing an Edge report; she asked Petra, MITI and MOF to clarify.
items.soWhat: A higher access charge would weaken corporate renewable deals that drive grid and cable orders.
items.watchOut: Not officially confirmed by the government at the time of the check.

items.headline: Masteel to buy 51% of HV electrical engineering firm Anpec for RM12mil to enter power infrastructure and data-centre work
items.detail: Anpec holds contracts with TNB and Sabah Electricity. Paid with RM3mil cash plus 45mil new shares at 20 sen; separate placement of up to RM5.78mil.
items.soWhat: A steelmaker buying into grid engineering shows how many firms are chasing TNB and data-centre power spending.
items.watchOut: Share sale agreement signed but completion pending; adds a new competitor for HV works.

items.headline: Southern Cable share subdivision listed 12 Oct; EPF filed near-daily substantial-shareholding changes 1-14 Oct
items.soWhat: The split raises the share count and may lift liquidity; EPF filings show an active institutional holder.
items.note: 16 filings in the period, mostly EPF substantial-shareholder changes. Direction of EPF dealings not characterised here.

items.headline: Epicon unit Concrete Empire wins RM47.38mil subcontract to supply precast segmental crossheads for the NPE Extension
items.soWhat: Highway work is feeding demand for precast (IBS) components.
items.detail: Awarded by IJM Construction to Epicon's 70%-owned Concrete Empire; works run from mid-November 2026 to end-November 2028.

items.headline: Cement up to 7.4% and steel up to 5.1% y-o-y in September (DOSM); steel eased 2.4% m-o-m to RM3,431.90/t
items.detail: Highest cement rise in Selangor, KL, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan (7.4%); steel highest in Perak (5.1%). Cement unchanged at RM25.80 per 50kg bag; cement up 0.3-1.9% m-o-m.
items.note: Official statistics.
items.soWhat: Input costs for precast and contractors are higher than a year ago, though steel is easing monthly; the Budget's variation-of-price mechanism matters.
items.watchOut: Margin squeeze on fixed-price contracts.

items.headline: International arrivals reach 28.8mil in Jan-Aug 2026, up only 1.8% y-o-y
items.detail: Tourism Malaysia frames this under the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign; says tourism contributes over 15% of GDP.
items.note: Article summary box says 2023; the body is dated 2 Oct 2026 and refers to this year.
items.soWhat: Volume is rising slowly despite the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign.
items.watchOut: Low growth rate; no hotel occupancy data in the source.

items.headline: Firefly extends Subang-Seletar cancellations to 16 Oct as haze worsens; Singapore PSI reached 127-203
items.soWhat: Haze is starting to disrupt short-haul travel, a near-term risk to hotel bookings if it persists.

items.headline: Budget 2027 gives tourism RM935mil (+RM235mil); Visit Malaysia extended into 2027 with a flight-route matching grant
items.detail: Grant targets new direct flights from China, India, Central Asia and Europe; Ecological Fiscal Transfer raised to RM270mil; Langkawi/Labuan duty-free limit to RM10,000 (48-hour stay). Hoteliers warn arrivals must turn into yield amid costs, Airbnb competition and luxury-room shortages in secondary cities.
items.note: Budget allocation; industry comments are views.
items.soWhat: New routes support KL occupancy and room rates, but profitability depends on cost control.
items.opportunity: Luxury hotels in Kota Bharu, Kuala Terengganu and Kuching are under-supplied, per operators.
items.watchOut: Rising operating and manpower costs.

items.headline: Genting Bhd proposes RM1.25bil rights issue, RM800mil to repay debt, as borrowings hit RM45.25bil
items.detail: 1H26 net profit down to RM74mil; gearing 0.51x from 0.43x, mainly from Resorts World New York City funding. Pricing at a 25-30% discount to TERP; major shareholders commit ~RM563.8mil. Completion expected 1Q2027.
items.note: Proposal, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.
items.soWhat: Malaysia's largest leisure group is deleveraging through equity; dilution for minorities.
items.watchOut: Subject to approvals; source reports profit decline percentages inconsistently.

sectorCoverage.aiTelcoIct: Core set checked 12-14 Oct: The Edge (Corporate, Malaysia, Highlight, Economic Focus, Tech flash; dates from article meta), TNGlobal feed, Malay Mail money feed, Bernama feed, NST business feed. Earlier-run items from company/HKEX filings kept. The Star: business and tech sections checked in the browser (paywall banner; some bodies shorter on reload); /property returned 404. MCMC not checked. Top-up search pass 14 Oct added regional press (Business Times Singapore, DealStreetAsia), Digital News Asia, TMR and Malay Mail items.
sectorCoverage.propertyDevelopment: Core set checked: The Edge (KPKT abandoned-projects item), Malay Mail, NST. Earlier-run items from The Star, EdgeProp and MOF kept. The Star /property returned 404, not checked. A Land 33 RM32.3mil land purchase (The Star) was not included because its body was truncated.
sectorCoverage.construction: Core set checked: The Edge, NST (Epicon, AWC and Gamuda also reported there; ledes only), Malay Mail. The Star: business and tech sections checked in the browser (paywall banner; some bodies shorter on reload); /property returned 404. Bursa: watchlist companies checked 1-14 Oct.
sectorCoverage.propertyInvestment: Core set checked 12-14 Oct (The Edge, Malay Mail, TMR, Bernama, NST feeds): no Malaysia retail-mall or retail-REIT item found in the window. The Star business section checked; /property 404. Bursa REIT filings not checked. Not evidence of no news. Top-up pass 14 Oct: an NST analyst piece on Budget consumer and property stocks was found but its body could not be read, so not included.
sectorCoverage.plantation: Core set checked: The Edge Commodities flash (global grains/metals only in window), Malay Mail, TMR. MPOB and Kenanga items from the earlier run kept. No new Malaysian palm oil item in the core feeds for 13-14 Oct.

keyTakeaways.headline: Johor data-centre money is getting bigger, and it is reaching contractors
keyTakeaways.soWhat: DayOne now has RM30bil of bank financing for Johor after a RM15bil top-up from seven lenders, including CIMB and Maybank, and PDG reportedly seeks US$1.2bil. The money is turning into contracts: IJM's RM1.23bil AT&S plant, MN Holdings' RM293.88mil HV landing stations, and AWC and Kinergy subcontracts in Port Dickson.

keyTakeaways.headline: Power is the bottleneck, and policy on it is shifting
keyTakeaways.soWhat: MITI's Privasia approval requires off-grid power, Hibiscus is pitching on-site plants for data centres, and Masteel is buying into HV grid work. A reported rise in the CRESS access charge to 18 sen/kWh (unconfirmed) could cool corporate RE deals. Cable makers like Southern Cable remain booked on DC and HV orders (analyst view). The government is also reviewing data centres' contracted versus actual power use and has floated requiring them to supply their own power.

keyTakeaways.headline: Housing: Budget helps first-home buyers and the abandoned-project backlog is clearing
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Stamp-duty relief up to RM750,000 supports entry-level demand from 2027, and KPKT says 1,726 sick or abandoned projects (RM158.16bil GDV) have been revived. Developers still flag building costs; the returning variation-of-price mechanism helps contractors absorb input swings.

keyTakeaways.headline: Palm oil: record stocks against a firm 2027 price outlook
keyTakeaways.soWhat: September stocks of 3.51mil t point to near-term price pressure. Kenanga still assumes RM4,700/t for 2027 on biodiesel and El Nino (forecast), while EU FTA palm oil terms are unresolved.

keyTakeaways.headline: Watchlist: GDB expands, Southern Cable splits shares, Pesona buys back
keyTakeaways.soWhat: GDB's proposed Sarawak acquisitions would roughly double its order book to RM741.81mil but come with placement and rights dilution (proposal only). Southern Cable's share subdivision listed on 12 Oct, and Pesona Metro filed 14 buy-back notices in two weeks.
